thread:
Alyssa (PM): heads-up — an enterprise customer asked us to accept both legacy `prompt` and the newer `messages` payloads on the same chat endpoint. They need function-calling and structured outputs to continue working. Can we put together a scoped proposal + launch criteria by EOD Fri?

Matt (Eng): quick q — are we talking about adapter-only at the API layer (translate prompt -> messages) or full runtime support for both shapes? adapter is much easier.

Alyssa (PM): my preference is adapter/router-level translation so runtime stays as-is. But we need to define canonical handling of roles, precedence for system messages, and how we treat assistant/system tokens that show up in prompts.

Jana (Platform): router adapter is fine. We'll want a feature flag per-tenant and telemetry to see adoption. Also need sampling for diffs so we can debug mismatches.

Matt (Eng): adapter can be lightweight, but edge cases are annoying: multiple system instructions embedded in prompt, explicit function-calling intent encoded in text, or customers relying on stray assistant messages. Need clear mapping rules.

Eli (Design): proposed mapping for docs: if client sends `prompt` (string) -> map to messages: `[{role: 'system', content: params.system || ''}, {role: 'user', content: prompt}]`. If they supply `system` separately, put it first. Provide examples in the migration guide.

Kai (ML): important: the same token distribution can lead to different decoded outputs when you change the role boundaries. We should require regression tests on prompt->messages mapping using both our canonical evals and any customer-provided eval sets. Gate the rollout on no major quality drops.

Sanjay (Sales): customers will ask for "no-behavior-change" guarantees. They expect identical outputs for their existing prompt usage. We can't promise bit-for-bit identity, but we should be explicit about the risk and offer assisted testing for large accounts.

Matt (Eng): agree — we can do deterministic mapping and surface a `compatibility_mode` flag. That flag pins the adapter behavior and enables expanded logging. We should also support an opt-out so customers can migrate gradually.

Alyssa (PM): draft launch criteria idea: 1) adapter implemented + feature-flagged, 2) 2-week canary (internal + opt-in customers), 3) automated regression checks pass on our eval suite, 4) docs + migration guide published, 5) telemetry shows <5% edgecase rate or we have triage plan. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Jana (Platform): ops checklist: add metric `compat.adapter.transform_failures`, add a sampled diff sink (1% of transformed calls) with PII scrubbing, enforce max prompt size per-tenant in adapter to prevent OOMs, and add quota bump protection for early adopters.

Eli (Design): migration docs should include: minimal examples, a mapping table for common developer patterns, and a small client-side shim snippet. Also call out known behavior differences and recommendations for system/assistant usage.

Sanjay (Sales): add a customer-facing compatibility worksheet we can run with top accounts — input examples, expected outputs, and a checklist for acceptable deltas. Offer special-assist migration for enterprise deals.

Matt (Eng): example adapter mapping (proto):

```
// incoming legacy payload
{ prompt: "Translate to French: Hello!", system: "You are a helpful translator." }

// adapter -> messages
messages = [
  { role: 'system', content: payload.system || '' },
  { role: 'user', content: payload.prompt }
]

// preserve function calling hints: if prompt contains explicit JSON instruction
// and customer set `function_call: 'auto'`, carry that field through unchanged.
```

Kai (ML): add: run prompt->messages translation across the main model zoo and compare top-k outputs and embedding drift. If drift > threshold, block rollout for that model family.

deploy-bot: feature flag `legacy_prompt_compat` created in staging. Reminder: add integration test and a rollout plan to the PR.

Alyssa (PM): great. I'll draft the RFC and an initial migration doc this afternoon. @Matt @Jana please add rough engineering/ops effort estimates by tomorrow so we can prioritize in the roadmap review. :thumbsup:
